name: bare count(*), 1M rows, WARM — O(1) from metadata, NOT a scan
claim: DIFFERENT KIND OF WIN, labeled honestly: a bare count(*) with no predicate is served O(1) from Basin's maintained row-count metadata — Basin does not scan the table at all. Neon counts by scanning. This is a real feature, but it is metadata lookup vs scan, not 'we scan faster'. p50 ms, lower is better.

note: These are NOT scan-speed numbers. A bare count(*) (no WHERE) is answered from Basin's maintained metadata in O(1) — the ~1.4ms is dispatch + wire, not table work. We separate this from the scan wins on purpose. A maintained-count bug (DELETE of an absent PK reported 'DELETE 1' and corrupted count(*)) was found and fixed this cycle with an adversarial oracle test, so this metadata path is now correctness-gated.
